page0.text:
Purification by holy word.
The priest's exorcism dispersed Zouken Matou's spiritual body.
Only two men are left in the clearing:
Kirei Kotomine leans against a wall, bloody and battered, his robes stained red.
Assassin is pinned to a tree by Black Keys.

page1.text:
"You completely erased my Lord Mage, Executor. Did you know he was a swarm of insects?"
...
He turns to face the voice.
Assassin is gone.
Only a blood stain and the Black Keys remain embedded in the tree.

page2.text: "...He and I go back a ways. I knew that he was a spirit who uses insects to interact with the world. Physical injury is ineffective. The only way to kill him would be to crush every trace of his body."

page3.text:
"So you attacked his spiritual body, instead.
He was quite attached to his mortality, but it made him vulnerable to the words of Scripture.
So that is why they call you an exorcist. You are Zouken Matou's natural enemy."

page4.text:
...
The priest doesn't answer. He checks his injuries.
His bleeding has stopped.
He's lost his weapons, but he isn't critically wounded. A few minutes' rest should be enough to recover his strength.

page5.text:
"What will you do now, Assassin? Your Master is gone. Even my prayers would prove effective against you, without his magical energy to support you."
"...Indeed. My body will soon fade away. Unless I find a replacement Master, I am little different from the spirits wandering these woods. In less than a day, I will regress into a lesser spirit and disappear from this world."

page6.text:
"That's right. Even an Executor such as myself can harm a Master-less Servant.
So, what now? Will you avenge your fallen lord?"
"I am not that impulsive. The Lord Mage was defeated by his own arrogance. It was no failure of mine.
There are still some things which do not make sense to me. I must know more about them."

page7.text:
"You mean how Zabaniya failed?
Your arm appears to be from a shaytan, but since you graced it with the name of a fallen angel, it cannot affect me.
As something that punishes humans, it cannot curse something of its own kind... I am no longer a man, and my heart is extraordinarily resistant to curses."

page8.text:
"...I knew it. Your heart is just like that girl's.
Have you already been tainted...?"
The priest doesn't answer.
His lips only curl into a sardonic smile.

page9.text:
"But how did you know? You would only have acted the way you did if you knew my arm would not affect you.
Did you intend to make me use my Noble Phantasm from the start?"
"Yes. I knew about your arm already, Assassin.
It is a cursed arm which creates an identical image of your target's heart and swaps it with the real heart by treating it as a mirror existence.
It is what killed my Servant."

page10.text:
"...! Then, you..."
"Yes, I was watching until his final moments.
So of course I knew. Your loss was decided the moment you killed Lancer."
"...Tch. What a failure."
Assassin clicks his tongue with loathing.
He dismisses his bloodlust.
Disappointed, he leaves. The priest's response seems to have satisfied his curiosity.

page11.text:
"...Gone to look for a new contractor, I see.
He will most likely serve Sakura Matou next..."
The priest has no problem with that.
As long as Zouken Matou doesn't kill Sakura Matou, he doesn't care.

page12.text:
Zouken wishes for immortality.
Obtaining Sakura's body will satisfy that desire.
As long as the old man is alive, the curse gestating within the Holy Grail will never be born.
It would be meaningless to have Sakura become an insect's vessel after she has grown this much.
He needs her to keep being a Master.
Because...

page13.text:
"Yes, there will be no eternity for you.
You were flawed from the moment you were born."

page14.text:
...
He feels slightly dizzy when he stands up.
He must be exhausted.
The priest leans against a wall, and sleepily closes his eyes for a time.

page16.text:
"Flawed from the moment you were born."
The man tried many things after he realized this truth.
In his youth, he did not understand morals, but he did possess common sense. He attempted to overcome this flaw.
But it was not to be.
His pain and struggle ended in failure.
His last effort was a woman.

page17.text:
It was a simple tale.
Any human dreams of loving someone of the opposite sex, having a family, and dying a peaceful death.
No one spurns that peace or fails to dream of it.
He was no exception.
Even if it didn't appeal to him at all, he decided that it would be nice to have,
and he loved a woman to obtain some measure of human-like happiness.

page18.text:
He chose a woman with no future.
She was ill, with only years left to live.
Did he choose her because of that, or because he had no other choice?
Even now, he's not sure why.

page19.text:
They spent about two years together.
The man tried to love the woman.
The woman did her best to love him back, and she gave him a child.
But the outcome did not change.
The man found happiness in his woman's suffering and his child's despair.
The more he tried to love her, the more she suffered. To him, it was the only saving grace of their bond.

page20.text:
The contradiction did not bother him. He is not even sure if he suffered.
But the more the woman tried to soothe him, the more he found himself wanting to see her grief.

page21.text:
She was a saint. She was frail, but he would have called her a saint.
It need not be said how profound her faith was, and how well she understood his rage.
That is why he nearly despaired.
He would never again meet someone who understood him so well and tried to heal him. But even this woman could not fill the void within him.

page22.text:
So, there was no need to question his life any longer.
He was born flawed.
His birth was a mistake.
He concluded that if he was a mistake, then he should disappear. He went to part ways with the woman before his death.
He married her as an experiment, so he was obligated to let her know it was over.

page23.text:
The woman loved Kotomine.
Kotomine tried to love her, too.
That's all there was to it.

page24.text:
The end came all too quickly.
"I could not love you."
He told her, in a room surrounded by stone walls.
The woman smiled on her deathbed. Her body, all skin and bones, could not even stand anymore.
"...No. You do love me."
Then she smiled, and ended her own life.

page25.text:
He didn't try to stop her. There would have been no point in doing so.
The woman had a terminal illness. She would have died sooner or later. He knew that when he chose her.

page26.text:
As her consciousness faded, the blood-soaked woman looked up at the man and laughed.
"See? You're crying, dear."
Of course, he didn't shed a single tear.
He only looked that way to her.
With her death, the woman proved to him that he could love someone, and that his life was worth living.
He left the room without saying another word, and abandoned the Lord's teachings.

page27.text:
...Yes.
He did think it was sad.
But not because she died.
In that moment, he thought...
"What a shame. If she was going to die anyway, I wish I could have killed her myself."
He did not mourn her death, but lamented the fact that he couldn't enjoy it.

page28.text:
It happened a long time ago.
He can't remember her face anymore, never mind her voice.
But sometimes, he thinks...
"I wish I could have killed her myself."
Would that have brought him joy?
Or was it because he loved her that he was sorry he couldn't kill her?

page29.text:
He would sever that train of thought whenever he found himself dwelling on it.
That question should be left to eternity.
The woman's death was meaningless,
because her devotion failed to change him.
But he did not want it to be worthless.
He would never try to answer that question.

page30.text:
...It happened a long, long time ago.
It was the memory of a man nourished by the misfortune of others, who found fulfillment in the world's corruption.
After that, the man met his archnemesis.
Kiritsugu Emiya.
A mage who chose to invalidate everything the man might have wanted for himself...

page31.text:
...
The priest opens his eyes.
It seems he was asleep for a while.
After confirming that his strength has returned, he begins walking to catch up to Shirou Emiya—

page32.text:
"You're not going anywhere.
No, you're going to die right here."

page34.text:
She has completely changed.
She is clothed in her own shadow.
Her dark magical energy cloaks her like a part of her own body.
The sheer amount of her magical energy and her existence are no longer that of a human's.
Her spiritual caliber has now reached the level of a pure Heroic Spirit, a Counter Guardian.

page35.text:
"...You've been completely corrupted, Sakura Matou.
Not just in body—you could not have transformed this much without adapting your mind to the curse.
So you've accepted that you are a monster, now."
The priest denounces her, even though he wished for it.
He scolds her for becoming drunk on her own power.

page36.text:
"...Heh. And what's wrong with that?
But I didn't have any other choice, you know.
Maybe I could have held out a little longer if people had been nicer to me."
"Oh? Held out against what?"

page37.text:
"Myself, Father.
I've finally accepted that I hate the world.
The Tohsaka family who abandoned me. My sister who's different from me in every way, living a free life. My scary grandfather and my pitiful brother. This whole town that doesn't know my suffering."

page38.text:
"I can't forgive any of them.
...I know I'm just taking my anger out on them. But I can't help but imagine this, even though I know it's wrong...
...Yes.
I wonder what faces they'll make when I teach everyone who's never helped me what it's like to be me."

page39.text:
The girl smiles in grim delight.
The priest is unaffected.
He looks at the girl like something dirty.

page40.text:
"You've changed, Sakura Matou... I see. Your nature was suited to the darkness."
"Yes, I've changed. I'm not the old Sakura Matou anymore. That weak girl is gone.
Everyone's always made me suffer. I'm just making them feel the same way. The girl who used to just put up with everything is gone."

page41.text:
She giggles.
Multiple personalities.
Sakura Matou is gone, replaced by a separate personality that was sleeping within.
It's the only explanation for her wildly different, charming attitude.
But...
"...What do you mean? There's no need to hide it, Sakura Matou."
The priest denies her with a blunt sentence.

page42.text:
"Huh? What do you..."
"I said you don't need to hide it.
You do not have a separate personality. You've become drunk on violence since the mud swallowed you, but you are still the same Sakura Matou. There's no need to invent a second personality as an excuse to show that you did nothing wrong."
The girl's face stiffens.
Is it true?
The blackened girl grits her teeth and glares back at the priest.

page43.text:
"What are you... You're the one who did this to me...!"
Her shadows writhe in concert with her loathing.
They erode everything around her like a blaze.
The speed with which her shadows covered the ground is nothing like before.

page44.text:
"I won't deny it. I allowed you to live so that you could become its Master. You've splendidly lived up to my expectations, and now you're trying to give birth to Avenger.
You've easily achieved something that I could not."

page45.text:
"It wasn't easy! You have no idea how much I've suffered! How much it hurts even now!"
"I don't know, nor do I need to know. I'm not eccentric enough to listen to a little girl's whining."

page46.text:
"Rrgh... All right.
That's fine. I don't want you to know, either.
I won't let you have pity for me that easily, because from now on, I'm the one who's going to be showing everyone else."
A cruel smile plays across her lips.

page47.text:
...
The priest doesn't hesitate to retreat.
He moves with the same swiftness that caught Zouken Matou in midair.

page48.text:
He only takes one bound away.
The girl is an amateur, despite her enormous magical power.
He can easily get away from someone who lacks experience in both combat and magecraft.

page49.text: "...Foolish man. Did you really think you could run from me?"

page50.text:
She snickers.
Instantly, the priest goes limp and tumbles to the ground.

page51.text:
"Guh...guoh...!"
He tumbles down.
Kirei Kotomine crumples, spewing something red from his mouth.
"Hargh...nnrgh, guh...!"
It doesn't stop.
He keeps vomiting blood, and each time he tries to fill his lungs with air, he coughs more blood.

page52.text:
"How does it feel to have someone grab your heart? Your life's in the palm of my hand no matter where you go, you know."
"Nngh...guh...!"
"Father, you died ten years ago. You died when Kiritsugu Emiya shot you through the heart. There's only one reason you've stuck around this long."

page53.text:
"You're his... Um, who was he again? Some Servant I ate earlier. Well, his name doesn't matter.
That golden man bathed in the contents of the Holy Grail and connected to that thing. But he couldn't be corrupted, so it flowed into his Master instead.
That's how you came back to life.
You escaped death because Avenger...because Aŋra Mainiiu gave you some of its power."

page54.text:
"Heh. I see. And that was..."
"Yes. You're connected to Aŋra Mainiiu. But I'm Aŋra Mainiiu now.
So I crushed it for you. I destroyed the black heart that's been keeping you alive.
If you want, I'll crush all your organs, too.
My hands can rip out your insides, no matter where you go."

page55.text:
The girl raises a hand.
Her gracious offer isn't sincere at all.
She has no intention of letting the priest leave alive.
She'll just laugh and kill him if he begs for his life.
She'll take back the temporary life that's sustained him.
After all, it belongs to her.
Even if the amount of magical energy he has is equivalent to a speck of dust in the corner of her bedroom, she doesn't need to let him have it.

page56.text:
"Goodbye. I suppose I should thank you for saving my life before, Father."
The girl's lovely fingers curl around an invisible doll.
There's a squeezing noise.
The priest on the ground is wrung out like a rag.
Just one more twist.
In less than a second, the priest will die completely.
But just before that...

page57.text:
"Nngh...! Argh, urgh, ahh!?"
The girl crumples to her knees.
...She's savaged by nausea and discomfort.
She claws at the blackened ground, as if pleading for help.

page58.text:
"Kuh...It hurts, no, don't...come in...!"
The shadows expand.
Something must have happened. The black robe covering her body suddenly blooms, before returning to its original size.

page59.text:
"No way...Berserker actually...lost..."
There can't be any other reason.
Berserker was defeated.
With his death, the pure magical energy of his soul flowed into the girl, the Holy Grail.

page60.text:
"...argh...Argh..."
Her mind twists.
Sakura Matou's personality is pushed further to the edge.
...There shouldn't be any more room, but a massive soul has her pressed against a wall.

page61.text:
"...Ah."
...She'll disappear.
She'll be gone for good.
At this rate, Sakura Matou will disappear."
"...Before...that..."
She remembers she meant to kill the priest and looks up. She curses herself for being too slow to follow through.
